notes: SHIP v1.14.405 - BLANK FORGE AISLE, PROVEN ROOT CAUSE. Found by a focused regression pass against the last device-verified good aisle (v1.14.353, 4f84c65, released in batch .351-.354 on 2026-07-25), not by another round of device logs. ONE FUNCTIONAL GUARD plus the stamp; everything else in the diff is comment. THE METHOD. Pickaxe over every commit from .353 to HEAD touching the aisle lifecycle returned exactly four: .385, .395, .401, .404. Extracting forge3d_render whole from .353 and from .404 and diffing them showed only FIVE functional deltas in a 1093-line function: the M1 store swap to safeGet/safeStore, the setStatus return value, .403's FIRST_FRAME trace, .404's repaint-after-loadout, and .401's RackEngine registration. The M1 store swap was checked for a get/set asymmetry - safeGet parses and safeStore stores the caller's string, so the pair is symmetric and NOT the cause; that hypothesis was killed before it was shipped rather than after. The traces and the repaint are additive and cannot blank a scene. That leaves .401's registration as the only delta that can destroy a working renderer. THE MECHANISM, and it is an interaction of three ships none of which is wrong alone. .391 gave bw_mount3D a BOUNDED RE-ARM - 12 tries x 400ms, roughly FIVE SECONDS of setTimeout retries - whose only liveness guard is document.body.contains(mount). .401 made context release SYMMETRIC: any renderer that registers disposes every other attachment through RackEngine.releaseOthers, invariant I1. Opening the aisle NEVER REMOVES #bw-mount FROM THE DOM, because the aisle is a separate full-screen sheet mounted as a direct child of #app, so Build's re-arm keeps firing for up to five seconds AFTER the aisle opens and every retry re-registers bw-mount and DISPOSES THE LIVE AISLE. The Forge HUD is static markup inside the sheet, so it stays perfect while only the scene dies. This accounts for every field in the device log without needing the unread entries: shell open, viewport blank, mountKids=0, mode=work, no AISLE_CLOSE_REQUESTED because nothing ever closed the sheet, and a surviving attachment of exactly [{host:bw-mount,kind:rack}] - Build took the context back. Before .401 the same re-arm was harmless, which is precisely why the aisle passed device verify at .353 and has been blank since; and .404 removed only the OBSERVER half of .401 and left releaseOthers untouched, which is why .404 did not fix it. .403's own comment predicted this exact signature: if releaseOthers disposed this scene because another renderer registered, that happens in teardown and the stack names the registrant. THE FIX - CORRECT THE GUARD, DO NOT ADD MACHINERY. The re-arm was asking the wrong question: is my mount still in the DOM is not the same as am I still the surface the technician is looking at. A retry loop that outlives a navigation to another WebGL surface is a stale callback. draw() now aborts when the aisle sheet is open. This ADDS NO timeout, NO retry, NO fallback, NO renderer, NO instrumentation and NO special case - it REMOVES work on a path that must not run at all. It sits at the top of draw() so that the first attempt and all twelve re-arms pass through one guard with no path left open. Not a silent failure: Build is not on screen, so a toast would fire over the aisle naming a surface the technician is not looking at; deferring is the correct outcome and it is recorded in the console. NOT DONE, deliberately: no route changed, no scene internals touched, RACK SCENE LOCK untouched, I1 NOT weakened - the single-live-context invariant still holds and is still symmetric, releaseOthers is unchanged, the aisle keeps its .404 observer exclusion, and no last-known-good restore was needed because the cause was proven in one pass. M2-b step 1 is preserved unpushed on branch m2b-step1-hold and is NOT in this ship. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, CSS braces 4557/4557 delta 0, line endings all-LF, PRECACHE untouched, three-stamp lockstep, functional diff is one guard. DEVICE-VERIFY, ONE PASS: clear the service-worker cache, confirm the app reports v1.14.405, open Build, confirm the rack preview renders, tap OPEN AISLE and confirm the AISLE DRAWS ITS CABINETS and KEEPS them for longer than five seconds - the old failure disposed the scene within that window - then walk the flanks, close, and repeat the full cycle ten times.
